# Robotics architecture index

Canonical B2 product documentation: <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning>.

Use this index to choose a workflow. Each linked architecture states its data flow, B2 zones, boundaries, and security model.

## [Offload robot logs from the fleet into a raw log lake](../architectures/robot-log-offload/architecture.md)

Robots record split rosbag2/MCAP files locally; an offload agent uploads each closed split to B2 over intermittent links, deletes the local copy only after the stored version's size and SHA-256 match the closed split, catalogs each session in Parquet, and copies incident windows into a separate Object Lock evidence bucket.

- **Audience:** Robotics fleet and data-infrastructure engineers, Field operations and site reliability teams, Security and safety-case owners
- **Problem:** Robots generate far more log data than site uplinks can carry and local disks fill up; engineers need a durable, cataloged record of every session without handing long-lived, broad storage credentials to every robot.
- **Workflow:** ros2 bag record writes MCAP splits, capped by duration or size, to the on-robot buffer → For each closed split the offload agent gets a short-lived presigned PUT from a site service (presigned upload-part URLs above 5 GB), or a depot or dock runs rclone for bulk or drive-swap offload → Splits land under `bags/<robot>/<session>/` → The site service verifies the uploaded version's byte count and full-file SHA-256, then acknowledges local deletion → A describe step reads rosbag2 metadata.yaml, writes metadata.json, and rolls the catalog/ Parquet index, inline or from B2 Event Notifications where enabled → Edge perception uploads only flagged frames and prediction JSON under `events/<robot>/` as triage signals → Incident windows are server-side copied into an Object Lock evidence bucket under `evidence/<incident_id>/` with a hash manifest → Lifecycle rules hide and then delete raw splits after the retention window; locked evidence is not removed by lifecycle
- **Expected scale:** Tens to hundreds of GB per robot-day across a fleet, uploaded in bursts when links allow. Standard B2 is the default; upload throughput is usually bounded by the site uplink, not B2. Use multipart for large splits and rclone for depot bulk offload.

## [Search, visualize and replay fleet sessions from the log lake](../architectures/fleet-search-replay/architecture.md)

Engineers query the session catalog in place to find sessions by robot, date, topic, or event, then open the matching MCAP or RRD files in browser viewers over presigned range reads, or download splits by presigned GET and replay them locally with ros2 bag play.

- **Audience:** Robotics software and autonomy engineers, Field triage and QA teams, Data-infrastructure engineers
- **Problem:** Engineers need to find the right ten minutes across thousands of robot-days without bulk-downloading terabytes of logs.
- **Workflow:** catalog/ Parquet holds one row per session or split with robot, time range, topics, ROS distro, and tags → DuckDB httpfs queries the catalog in place on B2 to select sessions → A service mints short-lived presigned GETs for the selected splits → The Foxglove app opens each MCAP over HTTP range requests, with bucket CORS for the Foxglove origins → Alternatively a self-managed Foxglove Primary Site with storageProvider s3_compatible indexes a B2 inbox into a B2 lake bucket → A conversion job writes .rrd recordings under `rrd/<robot>/<session>/` with the Rerun SDK; the Rerun Web Viewer loads them from presigned URLs → ros2 bag play replays a session locally after downloading its splits from a presigned GET manifest
- **Expected scale:** Interactive range reads over multi-GB MCAP files by a few to hundreds of engineers. Standard B2 is the default. Put a local NVMe cache in front of repeated replays of the same sessions; consider Overdrive only for sustained bulk re-processing.

## [Record teleoperation demonstrations and stream imitation-learning datasets](../architectures/teleop-imitation-datasets/architecture.md)

Teleop episodes are written in the LeRobot v3 layout or as Zarr replay buffers under versioned dataset prefixes on B2, curated in place, frozen as immutable versions, and streamed to trainers with ranged GETs instead of full downloads.

- **Audience:** Robot learning and imitation-learning researchers, Teleoperation and data-collection operations teams, ML platform engineers
- **Problem:** Demonstration datasets grow to TB scale; training many workers from a hub or local disk copies does not scale, and released dataset versions must stay reproducible.
- **Workflow:** Leader-follower, VR, or spacemouse teleop records episodes into the workstation buffer → Closed episodes are written to `drafts/<name>/`; curation writes each release to `datasets/<name>/<version>/` with meta/, data/chunk-*/, and `videos/<camera>/chunk-*/` → Daft reads LeRobot datasets lazily from s3:// for filtering, relabeling, and quality checks; Zarr replay buffers are read through s3fs → The curated version is frozen under its version prefix; DVC can optionally track it, storing its own content-addressed copy under `dvc/` → Trainers read meta/episodes Parquet, then make ranged GETs for only the data rows and MP4 byte ranges each episode needs, split across workers → Presigned GETs serve episode MP4s to review UIs
- **Expected scale:** Thousands to millions of episodes with multi-camera MP4 and Parquet state/action shards, read by many training workers. Standard B2 is the default. Ranged reads keep per-epoch transfer proportional to what is used; consider Overdrive for sustained multi-node streaming, and a local cache for repeated epochs on the same version.

## [Generate simulation rollouts and synthetic demonstrations at scale](../architectures/sim-rollout-datasets/architecture.md)

Parallel simulation workers load shared USD and MJCF assets from B2 and write each completed episode (video, state/action/reward arrays, summary JSON) to an append-only run prefix used for behavioral cloning, offline RL, and evaluation baselines.

- **Audience:** Simulation and sim-to-real engineers, Reinforcement-learning researchers, ML platform engineers running GPU sim farms
- **Problem:** Simulation sweeps produce millions of small and medium episode artifacts across many workers; teams need a shared asset source and a durable sink without a shared filesystem.
- **Workflow:** USD and MJCF assets live under sim-assets/; Isaac Sim can load them through an asset region profile pointed at the B2 endpoint → Ray or the cluster scheduler fans rollout workers out across GPUs → Each worker writes only completed episodes to `rollouts/<env>/<policy>/<run_id>/episode-<n>/` plus a run config.json → Simulator outputs written in place (for example HDF5) are closed locally, then synced to B2 with rclone as immutable files → Presigned GETs feed dataset explorers and review → Lifecycle rules expire scratch sweeps and purge hidden versions under rollouts/; promoted runs are server-side copied into datasets/
- **Expected scale:** Millions of small and medium episode objects per sweep written by many concurrent workers. Standard B2 is the default. Batch small arrays per episode instead of one object per step; consider Overdrive only when sustained sweep writes or reads saturate Standard throughput.

## [Train and evaluate robot policies, checkpoint runs, and release models to the fleet](../architectures/policy-training-registry/architecture.md)

Distributed visuomotor and VLA policy training streams data from B2 and writes checkpoints for fault-tolerant resume; runs and eval artifacts are tracked with lineage to dataset versions, and promoted policies are copied to a locked release prefix that robots and CI pull by presigned GET.

- **Audience:** Robot learning and ML platform engineers, Evaluation and release engineers, Fleet software teams
- **Problem:** Checkpoints range from hundreds of MB to tens of GB and accumulate across many runs; teams need resume after preemption, reproducible dataset-to-policy-to-eval lineage, and a controlled path for shipping models to the fleet.
- **Workflow:** Trainers stream WebDataset shards or LeRobot v3 episodes from B2 → Ray Train storage_path with endpoint_override writes `checkpoints/<run_id>/`; CheckpointConfig(num_to_keep=K) prunes older checkpoints → MLflow (b2:// artifact root) or ClearML records runs and artifacts; W&B reference artifacts track dataset and checkpoint lineage without copying bytes → Candidate policies run sim benchmark suites; eval videos and metrics go to `eval/<policy_version>/<suite>/` → Promoted checkpoints are server-side copied to `models/<policy>/<version>/` in an Object Lock bucket with retention set → A fleet release service mints presigned GETs for each release file; robots and CI download with them and hold no B2 keys; base VLA weights are cached once in B2 with hf-cache-sync → Lifecycle rules clean up hidden versions and abandoned run prefixes
- **Expected scale:** Multi-GB checkpoints written periodically by multi-node GPU jobs, plus eval video per candidate. Standard B2 is the default. Checkpoint writes are bursty multipart uploads; consider Overdrive when many nodes read training data in parallel for sustained periods, and stage to local NVMe for repeated epochs.

## [Archive LiDAR mapping sessions and publish site maps to robots](../architectures/mapping-session-archive/architecture.md)

LiDAR scans from mobile robots are archived per session; odometry and point-cloud jobs write poses, map snapshots, and trajectories beside the raw scans, and approved site maps are promoted to versioned prefixes that robots and RViz pull by presigned GET.

- **Audience:** Mapping and localization engineers, Mobile-robot deployment teams, Perception data engineers
- **Problem:** Re-mapping sites, updating localization maps, and debugging drift all need raw scans and every derived artifact kept together per session at GB to TB per site, without a shared filesystem.
- **Workflow:** Scans upload to `scans/<robot_id>/<session_id>/` by presigned PUT, with multipart for large map snapshots → KISS-ICP jobs write poses, `maps/<session_id>/map_*.ply`, and `trajectories/<session_id>/` next to an index.json → Open3D jobs downsample, register, and mesh under `jobs/<id>/` with JSON manifests and presigned previews → Approved site maps are server-side copied to `sitemaps/<site>/<version>/` and served to robots and RViz by presigned GET → Rejected or re-mapped sessions are deleted by version (ListObjectVersions, then DeleteObjects with VersionId), or hidden and purged by a daysFromHidingToDeleting lifecycle rule; lifecycle rules also expire intermediate job outputs
- **Expected scale:** GB to TB of scans per site, with periodic re-mapping and many robots pulling the current site map. Standard B2 is the default; site maps are small relative to scans and can be cached on the robot or at the site.
